result.title: ALIVE: Bring Foundation Features to Life with Events
result.summary: Visual foundation models provide powerful representations for diverse tasks, but their features become stale as visual content changes between image observations. Refreshing them requires new frames and repeated runs of a computationally expensive image encoder. We introduce ALIVE, an event-based method that incrementally updates native foundation model features between image observations. Given an anchor image, ALIVE uses subsequent events to transport and correct existing multi-layer features extracted by a frozen DINOv3 encoder. Its lightweight updater is trained end-to-end using only synthetic data, without downstream task supervision, and transfers directly to real-world event streams without any adaptation. Across three real-world datasets and five task-dataset settings spanning object detection, semantic segmentation, and depth estimation, ALIVE outperforms all evaluated event-based methods in every metric. On DSEC, when the anchor frame is 200,ms old, ALIVE improves over anchor-image predictions by 30.9,mAP in detection, 11.6,mIoU in segmentation, and 15.9% in depth AbsRel. Compared with image re-encoding, ALIVE reduces FLOPs by 82.4% and latency by a factor of 2.5.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ALIVE，利用两次图像观测之间的事件流，将冻结 DINOv3 编码器已提取的多层特征进行搬运与校正，并用纯合成数据端到端训练一个轻量更新器，从而无需重跑图像编码器即可增量刷新视觉特征。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「冻结编码器 + 轻量增量更新」维持视觉特征新鲜度的做法，可能为 LVR 中在不重复昂贵视觉编码的前提下持续更新内部视觉状态、以及动态计算成本核算提供可核查线索；但依赖事件相机输入，与推理/答案使用环节的联系尚待判断。
